items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: which Peggy Lee was doing with Benny Goodman

ctx.x: Now, just to follow through this a little bit, as far as comparing some of the leaders that you've mentioned so far. Tiny Bradshaw. What was he like?

Well, he was like a Lucky Millinder - Cab Calloway type. He didn't know any music, he was just a showman. And he had a person that was in charge of the band and he (Tiny) was out in front, you know what I mean, and I'll never forget Tiny--God rest his soul, he's gone now--but we did a tour in the South and I became aware of jealousy and envy and things. I wasn't even aware of this, but Lil Green was very popular in the South. People loved her, her recordings of "In the Dark" and "Why Don't You Do Right?" which…
come to see her, they'd seen Tiny for years, you know. But other than that, Tiny, he was alright. He never said anything to nobody, he just wanted you to play, you know. Yeah.
